Curriculum Leader for Drama
Deputy Headteacher/Drama Teacher
KS4 Exam Board: Edexcel
At Lynch Hill Enterprise Academy, Drama is important because:
1. Develops Communication Skills Drama helps students improve their speaking, listening, and non-verbal communication skills. Through acting and performance, they learn how to express ideas clearly and confidently.
2. Builds Creativity and Imagination Drama encourages students to think creatively, explore different perspectives, and use their imagination to create characters, stories, and solutions to problems.
3. Enhances Confidence and Teamwork Participating in drama activities helps students gain self-confidence by performing in front of others. It also teaches collaboration, as students must work together to rehearse, plan, and present performances successfully.
Our curriculum is designed to:
In Drama, we deliver the curriculum so:
The Edexcel GCSE Drama course is assessed through three components:
1. Component one; (Devising Theatre) Students create and perform an original piece from a stimulus and complete a devising portfolio. 40%
2. Component two; (Performing from a text) Students perform two extracts from a published play to a written examiner. 20%
3. Component three; (Theatre makers in practice) This is the written examination on a set text and evaluation of a live theatre performance. 40%
We know our curriculum is successful when students develop the following:

Special Educational Needs (SEN)
Slough's Local Offer provides information online about services, support and activities for children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) aged 0-25. Slough's Local Offer website has Google Translator and Browse Aloud to translate and read webpages with customise options to suit individual needs or preferences.
For people who do not have access to internet, Slough's Local Offer information can be found in a number of other ways. The Family Information Service offers a 9am -5pm telephone service on 01753 476589 and they can post or email the required information. You can speak to us at our regular outreach sessions which are held in the community venues such as libraries or schools. The Local Offer can be viewed on line at your local library.
Slough's Local Offer | Slough For You (sloughfamilyservices.org.uk)
The SEND information, advice and support service (SENDIASS) offers confidential, impartial, individualised support and advice on the steps to take in areas of education, health and social care to empower those who seek our assistance. The service is open to children and young people with special educational needs or disabilities, their parents and carers and professionals supporting them within education settings.
https://www.sloughsendiass.org.uk/
GEMS - free ADHD and Autism support across East Berkshire.
GEMS offers information & support to parents & carers of children with, or likely to have autism &/or ADHD within East Berkshire.
More details about GEMS workshops and social activities can be found via the following link: https://www.gems4health.com/workshops/
Should you wish to book a space please contact them promptly as spaces are filling up fast.
For further details, please contact GEMS directly. Call: 01753 373244 / 0800 999 1342 Email: gems.4health@nhs.net

An Interim Executive Board has been established to provide the necessary leadership and accountability to support the school’s improvement journey over the next 12 months. This is a strategic response to the school’s involvement in the RISE (Regional Improvement for Standards and Excellence programme) and will ensure the following is in place:
· Stronger strategic leadership and accountability
· Improved oversight of school improvement efforts
· Enhanced credibility with external stakeholders, including the RISE team
· Opportunity to build a more skilled and effective governance team
This arrangement will be reviewed in January 2027.
Queries about the management of Lynch Hill Enterprise Academy and the progress of any individual child should be directed in the first instance to the school.
Any written communication for the Chair of Governors should be sent to the school Reception marked for the attention of Ms J Smith.

Clubs and Activities
At Lynch Hill Enterprise Academy, we believe in enriching learning beyond the classroom.
“Pupils explore their interests and talents through the many extracurricular opportunities on offer, which are fully inclusive.” (Ofsted, March 2023)
Our extracurricular programme offers students a vibrant mix of clubs and activities that extend learning far beyond the classroom. Sports clubs cater to all ability levels and encourage participation, resilience, and growth. Students can also develop physical confidence, team spirit, and a healthy lifestyle.
In addition to sports, our enrichment opportunities include a wide range of interest-based clubs designed to spark curiosity and creativity. Each one fostering skills such as problem-solving, collaboration, and strategic thinking. With something for everyone, our clubs support personal development, wellbeing, and a sense of belonging within the school community.

pageCache.pageTitle: Student Mental Health & Wellbeing - Lynch Hill Enterprise Academy
pageCache.text:
Student Mental Health & Wellbeing
On this page you will find a variety of links to web pages, which you may find helpful, especially if you are experiencing lots of different emotions, that seem to change like the wind and feel difficult to cope with.
Hopefully you find some comfort in some of the websites we’ve included, with the aim to help you make sense of, and accept how you and your loved ones might be feeling as well as giving you ideas on what you can do to help you cope with the on-going situation.
If you’re really struggling you can always contact Ms Golden, Ms Flegg or Ms Bariya and arrange an appointment. You can also contact one of the school counsellors, for an informal chat on the phone or a video counselling session.
Remember if you need someone to talk to immediately then you can call Childline on 0800 1111 or click on one of the support services below:
Kooth Online Mental Wellbeing Community
